title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a definitions page that sets up categories of 'De Rham structures with divided powers', presumably for the 1976 IHES talk on the PD De Rham complex.

(1) A De Rham structure (divided powers understood) is a commutative bigraded ring A = ⊕A^{ij}.
- i is the total degree and j the exterior degree.
- A^{ij} ≠ 0 forces 0 ≤ j ≤ i. The complementary degree i−j ≥ 0 plays the role of polynomial weight.
- The ring is graded-alternating for the exterior degree.

(2) There is a differential d of bidegree (0,1). It is a derivation for the exterior degree: d(xy) = (dx)y + (−1)^{ext deg x} x dy. The model is the PD De Rham complex of a PD polynomial algebra, where x^{[n]} lies in A^{n,0} and x^{[n−1]}dx lies in A^{n,1}. So d keeps the total degree and raises the form degree.

(3) There are divided powers on the augmentation ideal A^+ = ⊕_{i+j>0} A^{ij}. They are compatible with both gradings (γ_d : A^{ij} → A^{di,dj}) and with d (d x^{[n]} = x^{[n−1]} dx).

(4) Since A^{1,−1} = 0, a degree-(1,0) cocycle T satisfies Z^{10} = H^{10}. Grothendieck singles out such a T. In general the cohomology along the exterior direction should be H^{*i}(A) ≅ h^i ⊗_k k{T}, with k = A^{00} and k{T} the PD polynomial algebra on T.

(5) A structure is special if three conditions hold:
- k{T} → H^{*0}(A) is an isomorphism;
- H^{*i}(A) = 0 for i > 0;
- every A^{ij} is k-flat (noted as useful for stability, presumably under base change and tensor products).
This is a PD Poincaré lemma relative to the PD line k{T}: a special structure is a flat, PD-acyclic 'resolution' of k⟨T⟩ in the exterior direction. Further conditions are added:
- flasque, a condition on the pieces A^{ij} for j < i (badly legible);
- universally flasque.
One speaks of a k-structure when k = A^{00} is fixed.

(6) On a topos X he defines categories DRsp(X,k)_0, DRspfl(X,k)_0 and DRspufl(X,k)_0. These are sheaves of special, special-flasque and special-universally-flasque De Rham structures, with morphisms respecting all structure. He then forms the categories of fractions DRsp(X,k), DRspfl(X,k) and DRspufl(X,k) by inverting quasi-isomorphisms.

The purpose appears to be a homotopy/derived theory of commutative divided-power De Rham algebras over an arbitrary base k (including Z or F_p) on an arbitrary topos. This would be an integral, characteristic-free analogue of Sullivan's polynomial-forms theory. It is plausibly a reaction to H. Cartan's contemporaneous axiomatization of cohomology theories via PD De Rham algebras ('Théories cohomologiques', Invent. Math. 1976). The expected theorem would compare these localized categories, presumably with derived categories or homotopy types of X, and show the three variants agree.
errors: The compatibility of divided powers with the alternating structure is not stated: for elements of odd exterior degree one needs x^{[n]} = 0 for n ≥ 2 (or at least x^2 = 0). γ_d is also only meaningful off A^{00}.

The general cohomology formula 'H^{*i}(A) ≅ [h^i ⊗_k k{T}, 0]' is ambiguous as written: h^i is undefined on the page. In the special case it reduces to h^0 = k and h^i = 0, which makes the general formula redundant or unclear.
The definition of 'flasque' is essentially illegible and incomplete (some condition on the A^{ij} for j < i). 'Universally flasque' is not defined at all.
The page leaves the ordering of the three localizations, and any expected equivalence between them, implicit.

ideas.what: Bigraded commutative PD De Rham algebra (total/exterior/complementary degree) with PD structure compatible with gradings and differential
ideas.modern_name: PD (divided power) dg-algebras / PD De Rham complex of PD polynomial algebras
ideas.where_published: Ideas behind crystalline cohomology appear in Grothendieck's 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (1968), but not this axiomatization

ideas.what: Special De Rham structure: flat, with PD Poincaré lemma relative to a PD line k{T} (H^{*0} = k{T}, H^{*i} = 0 for i > 0)
ideas.modern_name: Acyclic PD de Rham resolution; analogue of Sullivan's polynomial forms ∇(p,•) over Z with divided powers

ideas.what: Categories of sheaves of special (flasque, universally flasque) De Rham structures on a topos, localized at quasi-isomorphisms
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy category of sheaves of PD cdgas / commutative cochain models over arbitrary base
ideas.where_published: Related programme of 'schematization' sketched in Pursuing Stacks (1983) and letters to Breen; not this construction

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a characteristic-free homotopy theory of sheaves of divided-power De Rham algebras on an arbitrary topos. It comes in three variants (special, flasque, universally flasque), each localized at quasi-isomorphisms, evidently aiming at an integral/mod p commutative-cochain model of cohomology or homotopy types. This 1975-76 attempt, distinct from Cartan's published topological version, is not documented in the literature.
missed.quote: DRsp(X,k), DRspfl(X,k), DRspufl(X,k) catégories de fractions déduites en rendant inversibles les flèches - NB on les dit quasi-isos -
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral commutative models for homotopy types (Mandell, Toën's affine stacks, Lurie, and recent work on derived divided-power or 'derived commutative' rings) face exactly the question of which commutative structure over Z suffices. A topos-level PD De Rham approach predating 'Pursuing Stacks' would be a historically relevant precursor.

deep.surprise_reason: These are definitional notes, close in spirit to Cartan's 1976 published PD De Rham axiomatics. The topos-level localized categories are an unpublished Grothendieck programme anticipating later integral commutative-model work, but the page contains no results.
transcription_corrections: Header: probably 'Cat. dérivées des Alg. de De Rham spéciales', with the struck 'à p. div. - sous' leading into 'Structure De Rham (à p.d. - sous-entendue)'.
The struck word before 'T ∈ Z^{10}' is not 'élément'. It looks like 'élimination(?)', crossed out.
In 'A^{ij} ≠ 0 ⇒ 0 ≤ j ≤ i' a struck symbol precedes ⇒.
'Structure de De Rham flasque' line: the condition reads roughly 'les ⊗_k k' A^{ij} ... pour j<i'. Mostly illegible; the transcription's version is uncertain.
The margin note reads 'Univ. flasque' with '→ flasques' beside the special conditions; there is also a struck margin formula.
'(y compris les structures)' is likely an insertion above 'respectent toutes les structures', possibly '(y compris les PD-structures)'.
